explanation: The full classification: the set of (n,d) with n, d ≥ 2 for which AME(n,d) exists equals an answer set. This is a faithful formalization of OQP 35. Restricting to d ≥ 2 sensibly avoids the degenerate d = 1 case. The AME definition (normalization, plus a maximally mixed reduction on the first ⌊n/2⌋ parties after every permutation) is the standard one; for pure states, ⌊n/2⌋-subsets suffice.
